detail.methodology:
THE METHOD, WITHOUT THE MYSTERY
Confidence should come with context.

DelayLens is designed to replay recorded journeys, including the wait at your stop. Supported departure times get an estimated on-time probability and a 90% uncertainty band, inferred from TfL predictions.

At each departure time, 5–14 usable trips use a 90% Wilson interval; 15 or more use a 90% run-bootstrap interval. Fewer than 5 usable trips show no probability or advice. Recommendations require at least 15 usable trips for that departure time.

01
Record TfL predictions

Capture TfL predictions over time and infer journey samples.

02
Replay your journey

Compare departures with trips at a similar time of day, including your walks.

03
Make the trade-off

Choose how much risk you accept. Less data means more uncertainty.

Single-leg London routes and weekend observations only. Arrivals are inferred from TfL predictions, not measured, so every figure is an estimate, not a guarantee. Fixture results are synthetic and do not validate this method.
